      <title>Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/crystal-palace-and-newcastle-face-off-with-both-in-search-of-season-kickstart</link>
      <description><p>Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive</p><p>Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/27/crystal-palace-rayo-vallecano-conference-league-final-match-report">became used to success under Glasner</a> and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. <strong>EA</strong></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/crystal-palace-and-newcastle-face-off-with-both-in-search-of-season-kickstart">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend</link>
      <description><p>Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/10/premier-league-top-scorers-2026-27-race-for-golden-boot"><strong>Premier League top scorers</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/18/ange-postecoglou-sacked-by-nottingham-forest-after-40-days-as-head-coach">marked the end for Ange Postecoglou</a>, the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/18/nottingham-forest-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">narrow defeat by Arsenal</a>, while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. <strong>Niall McVeigh</strong></p><p><em>Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm </em><em>BST</em></p><p><em>Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST</em></p><p><em>Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST</em></p><p><em>Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Arsenal have beaten Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Leeds this season thanks to goals from players off the bench</p><p><strong>By </strong><a href="https://theanalyst.com/"><strong>Opta Analyst</strong></a></p><p>They say that once is an accident, twice is a coincidence and three times is a pattern.
